scenes.text: Have you ever zoomed in on your GPS and noticed a mysterious street that does not actually exist in real life?
Mapmakers call them trap streets, and they are secretly designed to catch sneaky competitors who steal data.
This actually backfired when a fake town called Agloe, New York was invented on a map, and years later, someone built a real store there because they thought the town was real.
Do you think Google Maps still hides secret traps today? Tell me in the comments and follow for more.
